hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse marks 165 years of guiding ships along Florida coast
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has been guiding ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years since its construction in 1860.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The striking red brick tower rises above the inlet, serving as a historic landmark that continues to draw visitors who want to experience its rich maritime history firsthand.

The lighthouse features a 105-step climb up a narrow spiral staircase to reach the top. Lighthouse keepers once climbed these same stairs night after night to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that shined for mariners navigating the coastal waters. The climb leads to the gallery at the top, where visitors are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views. The Atlantic Ocean stretches to the east, while below, the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers. Boats can be seen gliding through the channel, and the sea breeze provides relief from warm Florida weather.

Beyond the tower itself, the site includes museum grounds with restored historic buildings that tell the story of this important landmark. The buildings provide information about the lighthouse's construction, which took place before the Civil War. Visitors can learn about the different eras of the lighthouse's operation, including its years serving as an active Coast Guard station. The restored structures help illustrate how the facility functioned throughout its long history and the people who worked there.

The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse remains open to the public, allowing visitors to climb to the top of the tower and explore the historic buildings on the grounds. The facility offers a chance to experience both the physical challenge of the spiral staircase climb and the educational opportunities provided by the museum exhibits. Standing at the base of the red brick tower or looking out from the gallery above, visitors can connect with more than a century and a half of Florida's maritime history and appreciate the role this lighthouse played in keeping mariners safe along the Atlantic coast.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as grocery prices rise 2.8% this year
cards.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, offering Martin County shoppers a lower-cost option as food prices continu.
cards.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, giving Martin County shoppers another option as food costs continue straining family budgets. Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have an affordable option close to their home. Cheryl Cooperman said grocery prices are getting expensive and changing the way she shops. She said they are the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she goes with what is on sale instead of just what they want, something they never used to do.

The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon, predicting prices are going to stay inflated and are not going to go down. They said having stores like Aldi for the average person is extremely beneficial because there is nobody who is not feeling the price increase.

cards.headline: Woman charged with inhaling nitrous oxide in parking lot of Port St. Lucie Police Department
cards.body:
A woman faces charges after police say she was inhaling nitrous oxide in the parking lot of the Port St. Lucie Police Department on Thursday. The incident occurred at the police headquarters in Port St. Lucie.

Officers discovered the woman in the parking lot with nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas. The woman was taken into custody at the scene.

Port St. Lucie police charged the woman in connection with the incident. The arrest took place at the department's parking lot on Thursday.

Nitrous oxide inhalation is illegal in Florida. The woman now faces criminal charges related to the incident at the police facility.

cards.headline: Park Vista Community High School football team aims for state playoffs after strong finish to 2025 season
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said the team felt good throughout the second half of that season and is working towards being able to carry that through the whole season. He said the team has all the pieces in place now and it's just about executing. The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said the team has to take it one game at a time and can't look past anyone. He said the Cobras have to handle business weekly and if they do that and do their job, that will get them in the playoffs. Senior Erik Lee said he feels like the team has the guys they need to get it done, but also has to put the work in to get there as well. Senior Justice Jones said it's going to feel amazing because he already knows it's going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

cards.headline: Hammerheads Cruise Past St. Lucie Mets 15-3
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets committed five errors and gave up 17 hits in a 15-3 loss to the Jupiter Hammerheads on Camp Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday afternoon.

Jupiter s
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets committed five errors and gave up 17 hits in a 15-3 loss to the Jupiter Hammerheads on Camp Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday afternoon.

Jupiter scored in each of its final seven innings at the plate, steadily pulling away after the Mets grabbed an early lead.

Antonio Jimenez put St. Lucie ahead 2-1 with a two-run homer in the third inning, his second home run in the last three games and his fifth of the season with the Mets. The lead did not last. Jupiter answered with four runs in the bottom of the third to go up 5-2, keyed by a two-run single from Max Williams and an RBI double from Nixon Chirinos.

Jackson Hauge trimmed the deficit to 5-3 with a two-out RBI single in the fourth, but that was the last Mets hit until Elian Peña singled with one out in the eighth. In between, Jupiter reliever Elier Morillo retired all 10 batters he faced, striking out seven.

The Hammerheads kept adding on, scoring two in the fourth, two in the fifth and four in the sixth, the last punctuated by a three-run homer from Chirinos off Caden Wooster.

All nine Jupiter starters reached base and eight collected hits. Leadoff man Luis Cova went 4 for 5, a triple shy of the cycle, while Williams finished 2 for 5 with a homer, three RBI and three runs. For St. Lucie, Peña, Branny De Oleo and Francisco Toledo each went 2 for 4.

Mets starter Christian Rodriguez took the loss, charged with five runs on eight hits over three innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out five.

The Mets (4-12, 37-45) and Hammerheads (7-11, 44-40) continue their series Friday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks 67th most stressed city in the US, 42nd for financial stress
cards.teaser: A WalletHub study released this month ranked Port St. Lucie as the 67th most stressed city in the United States and 42nd most financially stressed in America.
cards.body:
A new WalletHub study released this month examined stress levels across American cities, finding that Port St. Lucie ranks 67th among the most stressed cities in the United States and 42nd for financial stress specifically. The study compared 182 cities using 39 different metrics, including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce rates and suicide rates. Among Florida cities, Jacksonville topped the state's stress rankings at number 37 nationally, while Miami came in at 50th and Fort Lauderdale at 83rd.

The report highlighted that Miami has the fourth worst affordable housing situation in the entire country. Florida overall performed relatively well compared to other states, with no cities landing in the top 35 most stressed locations. The study provides insight into how geography and local conditions affect the mental wellbeing of residents across different American communities.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo explained that while some stress comes from factors beyond our control, such as issues with family, friends or employers, location plays a significant role in stress levels. "Cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. When moving, it's important to consider how a certain city may impact your mental health, not just your financial opportunities," Lupo said. The analysis found that money, health and the economy continue to be the top sources of stress for Americans.

The five most stressed cities in the nation were Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana. On the opposite end of the spectrum, Fremont, California emerged as the least stressed city in America. Located in the Bay Area, Fremont is a notably affluent community with average home prices around $1.5 million. Following Fremont on the list of least stressed cities were South Burlington, Vermont, and two North Dakota cities, Bismarck and Fargo. The contrast between the most and least stressed cities suggests that economic stability, housing affordability and local infrastructure play crucial roles in determining resident stress levels across the country.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff in dramatic Wimbledon semifinal tiebreaker
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
hero.body:
Muchova became the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova ended Gauff's run with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.

Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, who was runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, who was champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, who was champion in 2024. For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August debut season
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League released the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women.
cards.body:
Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The league also includes the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois and games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium. The season will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. Whitmore said this is every little girl's dream to play professional baseball.

The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as 'Firebelle,' who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the 'Queen of the Diamond.' The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach in November, according to an announcement from Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The festival is scheduled to take place along the waterfront in Vero Beach.

The event has become an annual tradition for Treasure Coast residents and visitors seeking fresh seafood and coastal entertainment. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. has organized the festival for nearly two decades.

Details about the specific November dates and venue location in Vero Beach will be released by the event organizers. The festival typically features seafood vendors, live entertainment, and family activities along the Indian River County coast.

Residents interested in attending or participating in the festival can visit Under The Sun Promotions for updates as the event date approaches. The Treasure Coast Seafood Festival draws visitors from throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties each year.
